measurement.operands: HALF weights and actual captured HALF input; FP32 accumulation; HALF transformer output and FP32 final logits
measurement.candidate: One warp per output row, 4 or 8 warps per block, __fmaf_rn with fixed __fadd_rn shuffle tree
measurement.scope: One original short token history; layers 0/12/23 at decode steps 1/16/32. Final output projection always follows all 24 layers. Identical operands repeated inside each graph create cache-hot microbenchmarks, not complete GPT timings.

timing_boundaries.eager_event: One operation bracketed by CUDA events; can include host launch starvation, not asserted as pure kernel time.
timing_boundaries.graph_event: Total device event interval for graph-nodes repeated identical operations in one graph, with graph scheduling/cache effects; per-node is amortized, not full GPT decode.
timing_boundaries.graph_wall: Separate event-free schedule: graph launch through stream synchronization; no host copy or output comparison in timed interval.
timing_boundaries.enqueue: Host time to enqueue operation/graph only; no completion implied and never subtracted from event/wall time.
timing_boundaries.exclusions: Weight load, actual-input capture, compilation, allocations, warmup, archive writes and output checks excluded. No background memory sampler. Fixed method order is retained; no end-to-end speed claim.

decision.next_stage: Only the three passing shapes may enter a separately gated development experiment over complete fixed histories and complete requests. Retain cuBLAS for QKV/FFN-in and all existing failures. Full-model logits, sampling/stopping, content and audio-quality checks remain required.
decision.rounding: Exact HALF-product sums diagnose midpoint sensitivity; they neither replace the cuBLAS strict reference nor establish content/quality equivalence. Reproducing cuBLAS's exact reduction tree is not a prerequisite for future quality-based evaluation.
decision.performance: No full-request speedup, latency fraction, memory saving or quality claim follows from the isolated measurements.

research.scope: Bounded arXiv discovery for GEMV and low-batch/single-query GPU attention; newer-result queries cover 2025-01-01 through 2026-09-20 where specified. Not an exhaustive systematic review. Relevance statements come from the listed original paper sections, not search snippets.

papers.title: FlashDecoding++: Faster Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
sections_read: 5 Heuristic Dataflow with Hardware Resource Adaption
papers.relevance: Shape-dependent selection of CUDA Core GEMV versus Tensor Core flat/conventional GEMM. Five fixed Sakura decode shapes are a bounded local search space.
papers.limits: Large LLM widths and A100 examples do not establish a speedup for width 512 on RTX 5060. Unified-maximum/asynchronous softmax was not adopted.

papers.title: FlashInfer: Efficient and Customizable Attention Engine for LLM Inference Serving
papers.relevance: Query tile size 1 uses CUDA Cores. Short KV requests without split-K can write directly to final output, avoiding partial-output workspace and contraction.
papers.limits: Attention proposal only; no new attention kernel measured here. The paper does not establish benefit for this head_dim=32 RTX 5060 configuration. Preserve stable softmax, full KV, FP32 accumulation and fixed graphs.

papers.title: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
papers.relevance: Recent example of matching kernel pipelines to specific hardware bottlenecks.
papers.limits: Focuses on B200/GB200, BF16 throughput, asynchronous MMA and tensor memory. No measured GeForce RTX 5060 single-query head_dim=32 result was established. Its softmax approximations and backward-pass optimizations are not part of this experiment.

papers.title: High-Performance Portable GPU Primitives for Arbitrary Types and Operators in Julia
papers.relevance: Reduction axes, coalesced access, thread partitioning and matrix aspect ratios should be tuned together.
papers.limits: Column-major Julia kernels; A40 Float32 matrix-vector results use 10^7 to 10^9 matrix elements. They do not validate the much smaller row-major HALF Sakura shapes, and do not justify adding Julia or claiming vendor-independent speedup.
